newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telecom bill seen before Congress Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telecom bill seen before Congress Thursday.

text.p: A much-waited bill creating Brazil's new general telecommunications law is likely to go to Congress on Thursday, a lawmaker said.

Rep. Inocencio Oliveira, head of the pro-government PFL party's contingent in Congress' lower house, said the bill has been delayed due to problems of constitutionality related to the creation of a regulatory watchdog.
He also said the bill will be placed on the agenda for special sessions of Congress slated to begin January 6.
The Brazilian government was expected this afternoon was to send the measure to the Chamber of Deputies for an initial reading by the lower house's science and technology committee.
The law would create a watchdog and set broad guidelines for Brazil's communications sector as well as detail how Brasilia plans to break up and selloff of federal telecoms giant Telebras.
Telebras is made up of a holding company, 27 local operating units and long-distance firm Embratel.
Last week, Communications Minister Sergio Motta said the government intends to privatize all of Telebras by the end of 1998.
